long_biography.plain_text:
Energy infrastructure has been the constant in Paul Prager's businesses since he founded a private energy group in 1990. The group developed and operated power-generation, commodity-trading and related infrastructure businesses, giving him an operating platform rather than a single passive investment. He also established ventures in fuel distribution and commercial maritime operations.

Prager carried that power-market experience into TeraWulf, which he co-founded and now leads as chairman and chief executive. Initially built around Bitcoin mining, the listed company is shifting capacity towards data centres for artificial intelligence and high-performance computing. Prager's economic interest comes through his shares and founder role. TeraWulf's sites, power capacity, equipment and market capitalisation belong to the company, while assets in his other businesses remain with their respective entities.
